title: Chapter test: Closures and Iterators
summary: Twelve questions on closures, the Fn traits and iterators. You need 70% to pass; you can retry and your best score is kept.

questions.explanation: The closure borrows factor; reading it afterwards is fine.

options: `move || drop(s)` where s is a String
questions.explanation: Dropping s moves it out; a second call is impossible.

questions.q: Why does this not compile? `let mut v = vec![1]; let mut add = || v.push(2); println!("{v:?}"); add();`
options: push is not allowed in closures
v is mutably borrowed by add until its last call, so it cannot be read in between
questions.explanation: Move the println! after the last call.

questions.q: When must you use `move` with a closure passed to `thread::spawn`?
options: When it uses variables from the spawning scope, since the thread may outlive them
questions.explanation: The compiler cannot prove the borrow stays valid.
